title: Native sandbox for generated skills and approved self-work tests (#352)
body:
## Issue Scope
Closes #352. Native Windows AppContainer execution for Python infrastructure, generated JavaScript skills, and chat/self-work test commands. No Docker or visible external application.

Every test run requires fresh approval of Mana's fixed 15/30-minute resource recommendation. Tests run in disposable workspace copies with approved dependency sources, offline .NET packages, bounded Job Objects, and Stop during preparation/execution. An exact failed sandbox command can request a separately approved unrestricted rerun with an explicit host-file/network warning; it never happens automatically.

Helpers monitor their owning backend and clean up processes, scratch directories and AppContainer metadata even if the backend is terminated. Native launcher builds and Electron packaging provision the helper.

## Verification
- Combined live Windows tests passed: Node/.NET isolation, Python private-file/network denial, script broker limits, approvals and cleanup.
- Backend-crash cleanup verified independently for Node and Python.
- Full native launcher suite: 1,478 passed, 28 existing skips, zero failures.
- Real native launcher ChatModel tests compiled and passed offline in AppContainer.
- Full backend suite, native launcher, builds, DCO, CodeQL and live sandbox CI all passed on e8876fcf06e04c808e46793e2680681045cdd1df.
- Three consecutive clean reviews completed, covering approvals/isolation, cancellation/cleanup, and deployment/integration. Any implementation change reset the count.
- Repeated live suite: 71 passed plus the separately run update-wait test. No remaining owned sandbox processes or scratch directories after the cleanup audit.

## Update And Copy Safety
Updates stage the complete helper and wait for active scripts before replacing it. New launches queue behind a cancellable gate. Gate-lock and temporary-directory deletion races have regression coverage; persistent unreadable scratch fails closed. Credential-bearing package-manager configuration is excluded from workspace, dependency and runtime copies. CI uses a dedicated SDK and package cache, without raising production resource budgets or skipping isolation tests.

## Separation
Python chat tools, offered-file handling and chart presentation remain in the separate stacked #1327 PR #1376. This replaces the #352 slice of combined PR #1365.

This change intentionally updates protected execution/approval infrastructure at the user's request; generated self-work cannot edit these guardrails. Commits include DCO sign-offs.
